texts: My friend's parents rejected his marriage because the girl belongs to a lower caste, even though she is a doctor and he is unemployed. What would Kabir say?
Ask not the birth of a man but his deeds; the sheath has a caste, the blade has none.
Two lines, please, about the foolishness of judging a person's worth by the family they were born into, when all are made of the same blood, the same breath and the same dust.
doha on how caste makes no sense because everyone bleeds red
caste pride, empty
doha pls: upper caste guy thinks he's better just because of his surname
At my cousin's wedding, the groom's family kept asking about our surname and caste before they would even sit with us. I felt tiny. Doha for them?
Born high, he thinks the sky is his; but the same mother earth will take him in the end.
Compose a verse on the man who takes pride in the status of his birth, looks down on those he calls lowly, and forgets that no one chose the family or the caste they entered the world through.
surname pride, nonsense
In our village the low caste families are not allowed to draw water from the same tank as the others, and yet everyone prays together on festival days. A doha about this?
The same warmth lights every roof, the same rain drenches every field; who made this wall between neighbours?
write a doha on untouchability and how silly it is
caste divide
Write a doha for those who consider some people impure by birth and avoid their touch, though all were born the same way, breathed the same air, and will return to the same ground.
bier, moth, caste
The moth does not ask the glow its caste, and the bier does not ask the dead their birth.
At the cremation, I saw the bier of a rich upper caste man and that of a poor labourer burn side by side, and a moth flew over both. A doha?
A doha about the moth that circles the glow without asking its caste and the bier that carries rich and poor alike, showing that death knows no high birth, and pride of caste burns away like a moth.
doha: bier, moth, doesn't matter what caste you are at the end
My grandmother, who spins on her spinning wheel every evening, was once refused water at an upper caste home, and she says the yarn is yarn, whoever spins it. Could you make a doha?
doha: spinning wheel doesnt care what caste the spinner is

Write a doha on the spinning wheel which turns in the hands of a woman of any caste and makes the same cloth, which clothes both the high and the low, proving that work not birth makes a person worthy.
spinning wheel, caste
The spinning wheel does not ask the spinner's birth; the yarn is the same for king and weaver.
The sage's old question: do you ask the caste of the swordsman or the worth of the blade? The source of the stream or the sweetness of the water? The birth of the saint or the wisdom of his speech?
doha about asking someones caste instead of what they know
In the interview they asked my caste before my skills, and I felt that in two thousand years nothing had changed. A doha for that?
Do not ask the caste of the saint; ask what he knows of the One.
ask knowledge, not caste
My neighbour keeps a bird in a cage and boasts of its pedigree, yet will not eat with the family of the man who sells him the grain, because of their caste. A doha?
cage, high birth
The bird in a cage boasts of its lineage while it cannot soar; so does the man who boasts of his caste.
doha: cage and caste, pride of birth is just another prison
A doha about the man who sits in a golden cage of caste vanity, thinking he sits on a throne, unable to see the bars, while the world outside is open to all who are free.
The shroud has no caste, the scales have no caste; at the last weighing all are equal.
shroud, scales, caste
doha: shroud and scales, in the end everyone is weighed the same

A doha on how a shroud covers the rich and the poor with the same white cloth, and the scales of judgement weigh deeds and not birth, so that the caste proud will find themselves lighter than the humble.

At my grandfather's funeral the whole village came, high and low caste together, the same shroud was put on him as on the poor man who died that week, and the doctor said scales would weigh them alike. Doha?
caste, untouchable lie
A boy in my school was not allowed to sit with us because of his surname, and the teacher said nothing. I want something for him
If the touch of one man can pollute, how pure can the maker be who made all?
doha pls on how caste prejudice is wrong
Compose a verse on a world where a man is called unclean by birth and kept apart from others, though the Creator made him with the same hands that made the proudest of the high born.
At the wedding feast the lower caste cook was praised for the food, but guests would not let him sit with them, though a fly landed on everyone's plate and dew fell on all roofs equally. A doha?
A fly sits on the king's plate and the pauper's alike, and dew falls on both roofs; who made the difference?
Compose a doha on the fly and the dew, which treat every man alike whatever his caste, landing on the high and the low in the same way, showing that purity is not a gift of birth.
doha: fly and dew don't care about caste, why do we
fly, dew, caste
I read a news item about a family that was refused service at a restaurant for their caste, and I thought of the ocean, which takes all the streams equally. Could you write something?

A doha on the ocean, which welcomes every stream, large and small, clean and muddy, high or low, without asking their origin, and so teaches us that the heart that is wide has no room for caste pride.
The ocean gathers every stream and asks no questions; why is your heart narrower than the sea?
ocean, birth snobbery
doha: ocean accepts all, but people judge each other's caste
Sand from the high dunes and the low alike, once crushed together, cannot be told apart.
sand, one caste
A doha on the grains of sand, some from the highest dune and some from the lowest, that mingle in the wind until no one can say which grain came from where, as all humanity is of one making.
doha about sand mixing together like all people really do
At the beach, my kids built a castle from sand and when I said, 'this grain is from the high dune and this from the low', they laughed. It reminded me of caste. Can you write something?
elephant, high birth
My uncle sits on his veranda like an elephant, enormous with snobbery, and shoos away a poor boy who came to deliver cream for being from another community. A doha?
The elephant is proud of its height, but a small goad rules it; so is the pride of high birth.
Write a verse on the elephant which looks down on all creatures from its great height, as a high born man looks down on those he calls low, though both have a small goad that will rule them.
doha: elephant feels high because of its height, like caste pride
Please write a doha on those who say they are of the highest birth, that their blood is pure and they must not mix with the lowly, though the same blood runs in everyone's veins.
An old man in our colony refused to attend a funeral because the family belongs to a lower caste, and said he would be defiled. I felt so ashamed. Doha?
pure blood, lie
Cut the veins of high and low, and the same red flows out.
doha on pure blood nonsense
doha: priest and washerman both have the same god, why does caste put one above the other
The priest wears his birth on his shoulders, the washerman wears his work, and the Lord sees only the heart.
Write about the priest who looks down on the washerman as impure, though the washerman cleans the very cloth the priest wears, and both are made of the same breath and the same dust.
In our village the priest will not take a glass of water from the washerman's hand, but he wears the clothes that same washerman washes every week. A doha?
priest, washerman, caste
A verse about the mirror in which the high born and the low born see the same face, with the same eyes and the same fears, though they have been taught to believe that they are not alike.
When I looked at the mirror after hearing my in laws speak about the lower caste maid, I wondered what difference they saw in the mirror. A doha?
doha: mirror shows no caste
mirror, caste
The mirror shows only a face, and no one has ever found a caste in it.
The yogi wanders with his one-string lute and asks no caste, for the Lord is not born of any family.
Write a doha on the yogi who plays his one-string lute at every village without asking anyone's caste, and sings that the Lord is found in every home and every heart, and not only in the high ones.
doha: yogi with a one-string lute, doesn't ask caste, just sings
yogi, one-string lute, caste
A wandering yogi with a one-string lute came through our village and ate in the home of a low caste family, and the upper castes were furious. Doha for that?
My daughter fell in love with a boy from a different community and my family is calling it a disgrace. I want a doha to show them how silly this is
Compose a doha about parents who break a young couple's hearts for the sake of the caste, as if the pride of ancestors were worth more than the love and happiness of their living children.
Two hearts met, and an old wall of birth stood between them.
doha on forbidding love marriages over caste
caste vs love
doha: mirror and shadow, caste is a shadow, nothing real
A doha on how caste is only a shadow, which the mirror of truth cannot reflect, for if you look at the face alone, you will find nothing but a human face that is the same as all the others.
I looked in the mirror and saw my shadow behind me, and realized my father's idea of caste is just like that, something that follows us around without being real. A doha?
The mirror holds a face, and the shadow only darkens it; caste is the shadow.
mirror, shadow, caste
At the village function, my grandmother was told to use separate glasses for milk because of her caste, though she had stitched every guest's clothes with her needle. A doha for that insult?
doha: milk and needle, the needle stitches all, milk doesnt know caste
The milk does not ask the milkmaid's caste, and the needle stitches the cloth of all.
milk, needle, caste

A doha on the milk that nourishes high and low alike, and the needle that stitches the garments of everyone without distinction, which both do their honest work without asking who is allowed to benefit.
birth, not worth
People at the party kept asking my husband about his family, his village, his gotra, and I could tell they were measuring where to place him. A doha?
He asks about the family you came from, not the heart you carry.
doha about being judged by your family background
Write a doha on the habit of asking a person his lineage before offering him a seat, as if the nobility of the guest were written in his ancestors and not in his own behaviour.
cleric, caste, pride
doha: the cleric also has caste pride, even though his faith says all are equal
The cleric at our neighbourhood prayer says everyone is equal but there are different rows for different families. A doha?
Please write a doha about the cleric who preaches that all are equal before God yet looks down on the lower born among his flock, and keeps his own community apart in the same congregation.
In the cleric's hall of equals, the rows were drawn by birth.
doha on the foolishness of caste pride
Dust on the high road and dust on the low road are the same dust, and the wind lifts them equally.
caste, empty boast
Compose a couplet for those who boast of their lineage and of what their grandfathers were, while forgetting that nobody carries inherited glory into the grave, where all lie as humble as the rest.
My cousin spent the whole dinner telling us about our great grandfather the landlord, until my father said, 'And what have you done?' A doha for dad's reply?
doha: the tongue has no caste and the forest has no caste, all are equal

A doha about the tongue, which tastes the same sweetness whether the hand that feeds it is high or low, and the forest, which gives shade to every wanderer, whatever his birth, a lesson in equal generosity.
I watched a woman of a lower caste serve food to a proud old man, and his tongue enjoyed it all the same. At the edge of the forest I thought, how absurd. Doha?
The tongue does not ask the cook's caste, the forest does not ask the traveller's birth.
tongue, forest, caste
My uncle puts a bright forehead mark on every day and says it proves our family is of the highest birth, but he cannot name a single good deed of his own. A doha for him?
The forehead mark declares your family but not your heart.
forehead mark, caste
doha on wearing a forehead mark to show your caste status
Write a verse on the forehead mark worn as a badge of high birth, a sign to proclaim one's caste, which cannot make a man better nor hide from the Lord the true colour of the heart beneath.
The upper caste man across the lane calls the lower caste families snakes behind their back, yet the venom is in his own words. Doha?
snake, caste hatred
The snake is not poisonous by caste, and neither is man; the poison is in the mind.
doha: a snake doesn't have caste but humans do
A doha on the snake which is never judged by its caste but only by whether it bites, while men judge each other by the family they were born into and never by whether they do harm.
doha: physician doesn't ask the patient's caste, cotton bandage same for all
A doha about the physician who treats the patient without asking his caste and the cotton he uses to bind the wounds, white and soft for all, teaching that kindness has no regard for birth.
The physician's cotton binds the wounds of the high and the low, and no one has found a difference in the pain.

When my father was ill, the doctor who treated him was from a lower caste, and some relatives refused to take his medicine, until the fever grew worse. A doha, please? The cotton bandage was the same.
physician, cotton, caste
What is the worth of a lineage that cannot feed a hungry child?
doha on rich families being proud of their ancestry
ancestry, worthless pride

Please write a couplet on the pride that clings to ancestry, the old names, the old land, the old titles, none of which will stand beside the one who lives with humility and truth in the here and now.
My distant relatives are always reminding us of our great grandfather's title, but they are broke and dependent on us for money. Doha?
stone, thread, caste
doha: stone and thread both are equal, caste is man made
The stone does not know its mason's birth, and the thread does not know the hand that measured.
A mason from the lower caste carved the beautiful stone for the village hall, and the same men who praised it would not share a meal with him. A doha that mentions the thread of his plumb line?
A doha on the stone shaped by a mason of low birth into a holy place, and the thread by which he measured it straight, showing that fine work is not made lesser by the caste of the maker.
door, peacock, caste
The family next door shut the door in the face of a lower caste friend of mine, while their pet peacock strutted around the yard like it owned the place. A doha for that?

A doha about the proud peacock which spreads its feathers at every door without regard to whose it is, and the high born man who closes his door to the lower born and thinks the closed door makes him taller.
The peacock struts through every door, the man of high birth shuts his against his neighbour.
doha: peacock walks through any door, but humans close doors on low caste people
doha about people changing their behavior once they learn your caste
The moment my landlord learned my surname he said the room was already taken, and I could see from his face why. A doha?
Compose two lines for those who greet you warmly until they learn the family you were born in, and then turn their faces away, as if the name of a caste could change the person standing before them.
When your name was spoken, his smile shrank to the size of his birth.
caste changes smiles
When the sacred dress and the sacred hair are taken away, all men stand as one.
stripped of caste, same
In the hospital waiting room we all wore the same plain gown, high caste and low caste, and nobody could tell the difference. It was strange and beautiful. Doha?
doha idea: strip off your name and surname and everyone is the same person
Write a doha on how once the titles, the surnames, the garments and the family names are all stripped away, a man is only a man, as naked as the day he was born, and exactly like the next.
The family that owns the grindstone workshop in our village is of a lower caste, and the others, who repeat caste talk like a parrot, still hesitate to eat from their flour. A doha?
doha: parrot and grindstone, the parrot repeats caste talk but the grindstone grinds all grain equally
The grindstone grinds every grain alike; the parrot repeats what it has been taught of caste.
A doha on the grindstone, which turns all grain into flour without knowing whose field it came from, and the parrot, which repeats its masters' proud talk of caste without ever understanding a word.
parrot, grindstone, caste
The cloth sheet covers the high and the low alike in the cold of the night; so does mercy.
cloth sheet, caste
On a winter night, a poor lower caste man was given a cloth sheet by a higher caste woman, and nobody in the street said a word. It made me smile. A doha?
doha: cloth sheet keeps all warm, doesnt ask caste

A doha about the cloth sheet that warms the shivering of any wanderer who is lucky to receive it, indifferent to his birth, and the open hand that gives it, which is the only true mark of a high family.
A doha on the beggar and the weaver at his loom, both judged by the families they came from, though the weaver weaves the cloth that clothes the proud, and the beggar teaches humility in his need.
The weaver's loom clothes the proud; the beggar's hand teaches them to be humble; neither is a matter of birth.
doha: beggar and weaver at his loom both treated as low caste but they matter
My neighbour is a weaver who works at his loom all day and a lower caste, and the beggar outside our gate gets more respect than he does from the proud ones. A doha about this?
beggar, weaver's loom, caste
parrot, caste talk
Please write a doha about the parrot kept by the high born family, taught fine words about purity and caste, which it repeats without understanding a single word of the pride it is made to carry.
doha: parrot repeating caste talk it was taught
The parrot at my uncle's home has learned to say the family's caste slogans, and I realized how much of caste talk is just repeating what we've been taught. Doha for that?
The parrot recites the pride of its master, and knows not what it says.
caste is man made

A doha on the idea that the Creator made humankind from one clay and one breath, and that the divisions of high and low, pure and impure, were invented later by men who wanted power over their neighbours.
doha: caste was invented by people, not by God
God made man; man made caste.
My grandfather always said God never wrote a surname on a baby's forehead, and we should not either. Is there a doha like that?
doha about being proud of your caste and doing nothing of worth
My cousin brags all day about his clan's glory, but he drops out of college and has never held a job. A doha for him?
He wears his ancestors like a borrowed crown.
borrowed glory
A doha on the fool who rests all his pride on the deeds of his forefathers, never doing a deed of his own, like a man who boasts of the harvest from a field he has never sown.
In our village a lower caste man built the little bridge over the stream, and the proud ones won't cross it, but they won't build their own. And the one-string lute singer crosses it freely. Doha?
one-string lute, bridge, caste
The singer with his one-string lute crosses the bridge, and the bridge asks not his caste.

A doha on the bridge that carries the high and the low across the stream with equal patience, and the singer with his one-string lute who sings of one Lord, while the proud wait on the shore rather than cross.
doha: bridge doesnt care who built it or who crosses, one-string lute guy crosses it free
jaggery, crow, caste
At the festival function, the jaggery sweets were given first to the upper castes and the crow that ate the leftover jaggery was shooed away from everyone. A doha for this?
Jaggery is sweet to the high and the low, and the crow eats it without asking whose it is.
doha: jaggery tastes sweet to all, the crow eats it, no caste

A doha on the jaggery whose sweetness is the same in the mouth of any caste, and the crow that eats where it finds food without asking about birth, teaching the proud something of ease and fellowship.
In the inn, high and low rest on the same floor, and the cotton blanket warms them all the same.

A doha about the roadside inn where wanderers of every caste sleep under one roof, share the same cotton blankets, and wake with the same morning light on their faces, teaching what the village never learned.
doha: inn and cotton blanket, no caste in an inn
inn, cotton, caste
On our long train journey, we stopped at an inn where everyone slept side by side in cotton quilts, and in the morning nobody seemed to remember the caste they came with. Doha?
tongue, caste insult
A doha on the tongue that speaks of caste to insult a neighbour and the lowly man who keeps his own tongue sweet, so that the high one is lowered by his words and the low is raised by his.
doha: harsh tongue about caste makes you low yourself
The tongue that wounds with caste has lowered itself.
A relative called our maid a low caste name at dinner, and she looked down, and my tongue was frozen with shame. Could you give me a doha to say what I could not?
doha: no one asks the caste of a doctor in an emergency
In the hour of need, no one asks the helping hand its birth.
Write a doha on how in times of flame or flood or sickness nobody asks the caste of the one who comes to rescue them, and how silly it is that they remember it again when the danger has passed.
rescue, no caste asked
When our building flooded last year, a lower caste neighbour pulled my father out, and now my father still won't sit with him. Doha?
My father said not to wear the shroud of caste to our graves, because at the end all the shrouds look the same. A doha for his thought?
doha: shroud has no caste
In the end the shroud is white for all, and no one asks which family wove it.
A doha on the shroud, which is the last garment of every man and woman, and which does not carry any caste mark or family name, a final lesson in equality that the living refuse to learn.
shroud, caste
doha: forest and crossroads, no caste there
forest, crossroads, caste

A verse about the forest where all the greenery stands together, tall and short, and the crossroads where all wayfarers meet, high and low, none asking the other's family, because the road does not belong to any caste.
In the forest all growth rises together, at the crossroads all feet meet; caste is a village thing.
I got lost in a forest with a stranger and we met at a crossroads, and he helped me find my way, and only later did I learn he was from a different community. Doha?
churn, caste
The churn takes the cream of any cow and gives butter of the same colour.
doha: churn works the same for all, butter has no caste
My mother-in-law refuses to let our maid touch the churn, and yet the butter itself is made by churning with her hands. Could you write a doha?
A doha about the churn, which is turned by hands of all families to bring the same butter to every table, and the proud woman who refuses to let a low caste neighbour touch it.
He who is born high and acts in a low way is low; he who is born low and acts with grace is high.
deeds make the man
doha on how deeds matter more than the family you are born in
The most generous man in our village is from a lower caste, and the proudest man gives nothing. People still bow to the proud one. A doha?
A doha on how a person is high or low by what he does and not by where he was born, since a good deed by a so called low person is above a cruel deed by the highborn.
doha: washerman washes everyones clothes and nobody asks his caste when the clothes are clean
washerman, caste scorn
The washerman cleans the clothes of the high born, and is not allowed to sit among them.

A doha on the washerman who cleans the garments of every family in the village, from the proudest to the poorest, yet is called unclean and kept away from the festivals and the feasts by the same families.
Our washerman's son topped his class, but at the school function other parents would not sit next to his mother. Doha for her?
Write a couplet on the great confusion of men who say they know the Lord and yet make divisions of high and low among his children, as though the Father had favourites among those he made.
doha on people claiming to worship God while divided by caste
At the satsang, everyone sang about universal love, and then the seating was arranged by family caste. I could not help but laugh in despair. Doha?
faith, caste hypocrisy
They sing of one Lord and sit in separate rows.

A doha about the cloth sheet that dresses a king in the morning and a pauper at night and passes from hand to hand without asking whose body it covers, because cloth knows no caste, and neither should men.
cloth sheet, caste
One cloth sheet on the king's shoulder, one on the pauper's: who has found the caste of the cloth?
doha: the same cloth sheet covers a rich and poor man, no caste
My aunt gave her old cloth sheet to a poor man at our gate and her husband said that the man was a lower caste, 'he'll make it impure.' I was shocked. A doha?
